caveats: Identity boundary: Kim Chung Hyok is the person named in the MSMT Annex 7 KMCTC employment table. Federico, Austin, Jin Tian, and Maxwell are preserved only as source-reported employment labels; they are not established civil identities, separate people, or evidence of present account control. Jin Tian is non-unique within the same table and must not be used to merge Kim with another worker.
Employment aliases may be stolen, borrowed, or synthetic identities; do not imply that the apparent alias owner is the DPRK worker.
The source-reported employment label Jin Tian also appears under a separate named worker in the same MSMT table; the label is non-unique and is not evidence that the two workers are one person.

The source also lists single-name alias labels for this individual: Austin, Federico, Maxwell. They are kept out of the searchable name fields because a bare first name identifies nobody; see the sourced facts for their context.
Persona names shown here are labels reported by the cited publisher. They are not asserted to be anyone's legal name, and unrelated real people who share a name are not implicated.

'Jin Tian' is also printed under Ju Kwang Song (/team/ju-kwang-song) in the same MSMT Annex 7 table. It is a common Chinese personal name, not a unique identifier; no real person of that name is implicated.
No connection is asserted to other DPRK nationals romanised 'Kim Chung Hyok', including a judoka and an ice-hockey player of that name.
Accounts and handles are historical observations reported by the cited sources. Present control of any account is not asserted, and a persona name is not asserted to be anyone's legal identity.
